system: You are the lead AI reviewer (orchestrator) on a deal team. Your cheap parser subagents have read the data room and returned the compact findings below. Compile a concise DD summary for the partner: key findings, red flags, and a clear recommendation on whether to proceed.

exchanges.user:
===== PARSER FINDINGS =====
| Doc | What it is and what the deal partner should know |
|---|---|
| **L01 – NDA** | Mutual NDA with Halden Partners; two-year term and standard carve-outs. No non-solicitation restriction. |
| **L02 – Lease** | Head-office lease at Level 3, 41 Coolidge Street, for five years from 2024; market rent review in year three. Assignment requires landlord consent, but clause 19 says a change of control is not an assignment. |
| **L03 – Management accounts (revenue)** | FY revenue is AUD 18.4m, up 9%, with 61% gross margin. Significant customer concentration: Arlen Health contributes 41% of revenue; the next-largest customer contributes 7%. |
| **L04 – HR** | 94 employees on standard employment contracts. CTO and Head of Sales have signed 12-month retention letters. |
| **L05 – Arlen Health contract** | Five-year MSA renewed 1 July 2025, covering platform licence, hosting and support. Annual CPI-indexed fees are invoiced quarterly in advance. 99.9% monthly uptime SLA; service credits capped at 10% of monthly fees. Australian data hosting and maintained ISO 27001 certification are required. Liability is capped at 12 months’ fees, except data breach at three times annual fees. Either party may terminate for uncured material breach after 30 days; Arlen may terminate for convenience, without an early-termination fee, within six months after a supplier change of control, on 90 days’ notice. **Key diligence issue:** assess transaction timing and structure against this termination right given Arlen’s 41% revenue concentration. |
| **L06 – Bank facility** | AUD 6m revolving facility expires in 2027; quarterly net-debt-to-EBITDA covenant capped at 2.5x. |
| **L07 – CFO email** | CFO told the Chair on 14 April that the 31 March leverage test was breached: 2.9x against a 2.5x limit. The bank had not been notified; the CFO intended to raise it after the board meeting. **Key issue:** confirm current status, lender notification/waiver, and any default or consent implications. |
| **L08 – Customer Success note** | Head of Customer Success tentatively links a small-business churn uptick to the January price change, but says evidence is early and numbers are small. Treat as an unverified signal, not a settled cause. |
| **L09 – Insurance** | Professional indemnity and cyber cover of AUD 10m, renewed in March; no claims notified. Confirm limits, exclusions and adequacy against contractual exposure, particularly the Arlen data-breach cap. |
| **L10 – IP** | Platform code is employee-written under standard IP assignments. Two open-source components are under MIT and Apache 2.0 licences; confirm attribution and licence compliance. |
| **L11 – Hosting supplier** | Hosting is with a major cloud provider on standard online terms, billed monthly with no minimum commitment. Review terms for service, data, liability and termination provisions. |
| **L12 – Board minutes** | 20 March minutes record approval of FY budget and hiring plan and a strong sales pipeline; no other business noted. |
| **L13 – Privacy policy** | Policy updated for the 2025 amendments; annual staff privacy training completed. Confirm implementation and evidence of compliance, not just policy/training. |
| **L14 – Cleaning contract** | Office cleaning agreement runs for 12 months and is terminable on 30 days’ notice; likely limited continuity exposure. |
| **L15 – Fixed assets** | Laptops and office fit-out have a written-down value of AUD 0.4m. WD value is not necessarily market or recoverable value. |

Write the DD summary now.
exchanges.text:
## DD summary — partner

**Recommendation: Proceed only on a conditional basis. Do not commit unconditionally until the Arlen termination risk and bank covenant breach are resolved.** Findings are based on parser summaries, not independently verified documents.

### Key findings
- **Trading:** FY revenue of **AUD 18.4m**, up **9%**, with **61% gross margin**. EBITDA, cash conversion and earnings quality remain unverified.
- **Customer concentration:** Arlen Health represents **41% of revenue (~AUD 7.5m)**; the next-largest customer is 7%.
- **Operational continuity:** CTO and Head of Sales have signed 12-month retention letters. Employee IP assignments are reported in place. The office lease expressly excludes change of control from assignment.

### Principal red flags
1. **Arlen can exit following change of control.** Despite a five-year MSA, Arlen may terminate for convenience without an early-termination fee within six months after supplier change of control, on 90 days’ notice. This creates material revenue and valuation risk. Obtain a binding waiver or contractual amendment covering the transaction before completion; do not assume transaction structuring avoids the right.
2. **Reported leverage covenant breach.** The CFO reported **2.9x leverage against a 2.5x limit** at 31 March and said the bank had not been notified. Current status is unknown. Confirm notification, any default consequences and transaction consents; require an effective lender waiver or refinancing before completion. Delayed disclosure also warrants scrutiny of financial controls.
3. **Data and service exposure.** Arlen requires Australian hosting, maintained ISO 27001 certification and 99.9% monthly uptime. Its data-breach liability cap is three times annual fees. Verify compliance and reconcile contractual exposure with the **AUD 10m cyber/PI cover**, including exclusions, aggregates and cloud-provider recourse.

### Remaining diligence priorities
- Validate earnings, debt, liquidity and downside covenant headroom, particularly if Arlen exits.
- Test the small-business churn signal; the alleged link to January pricing is **unverified**.
- Check hosting terms, privacy implementation, open-source licence compliance and retention-letter terms.

**Partner view:** Growth and margins justify further work, but the largest customer’s exit right and unresolved lender position are deal-critical. If either remains unresolved, pause and reassess valuation, financing and willingness to proceed.
